incidents.title: The feed is down.
incidents.brief: A traffic spike just hit a single overloaded server. Users can't refresh their feeds.
incidents.constraint: Requests queue and the same server handles all work.
incidents.question: What should we add?

choices.label: More servers
choices.resultBody: Identical stateless servers now share the spike. Next you will need a real load balancer so routing stays even.

choices.label: Bigger machine
choices.resultBody: One bigger box still has one blast radius. Vertical scale delays the crash; it does not remove it.

choices.label: Longer timeout
choices.resultBody: Clients wait longer on the same saturated process. Timeouts hide overload; they do not add capacity.

hints: Work is stuck on one box.

incidents.title: Nightly import burst
incidents.brief: A nightly job sends 12,000 API requests in 30 seconds and one server sits saturated.
incidents.constraint: The services are stateful on a single node.
incidents.question: What reduces failure risk?

choices.label: Stateless fleet
choices.resultBody: Stateless workers behind a shared entry point can absorb the burst.

choices.label: Bigger VM
choices.resultBody: A larger VM is still a single point of failure for the import.

choices.label: Longer queue
choices.resultBody: A deeper queue hides the saturation. It does not add consumers.

hints: Copies cannot join until state is external.

incidents.title: Microservice rollout
incidents.brief: A new microservice jumps from 500 to 15,000 req/s on one instance.
incidents.constraint: Only one service instance exists and it hits CPU limits.
incidents.question: What should happen next?

choices.label: More instances
choices.resultBody: Add identical instances and route work across them.

choices.label: One backup
choices.resultBody: A single backup is failover, not capacity.

choices.label: DB-first
choices.resultBody: Moving logic into the database does not add app CPU.

hints: Copies of the same service share load.

incidents.title: Background worker backlog
incidents.brief: Image processing queue grows faster than a single worker drains it.
incidents.constraint: One worker is overloaded while others are idle.
incidents.question: Which model restores capacity?

choices.label: More workers
choices.resultBody: Multiple workers pulling the same queue drain the backlog.

choices.label: One consumer
choices.resultBody: One consumer cannot outrun a growing queue.

choices.label: More retries
choices.resultBody: Retries add work. They do not add workers.

hints: The queue can feed many consumers.

incidents.title: API traffic from one region
incidents.brief: Traffic grew from 1k to 20k req/s but all users hit the same instance.
incidents.constraint: The rest of the fleet does almost no work.
incidents.question: What is the mismatch?

choices.label: Spread traffic
choices.resultBody: Send traffic across the fleet so idle instances actually work.

choices.label: Change code
choices.resultBody: A code tweak does not move sockets off the hot box.

choices.label: Stronger box
choices.resultBody: A stronger machine leaves the fleet idle.

hints: One entry target is the bug.

incidents.title: One crash takes the service down
incidents.brief: Sessions live in process memory. When the process dies, everyone is logged out.
incidents.constraint: The system is not stateless and cannot be rebuilt quickly.
incidents.question: What is the design issue?

choices.label: External sessions
choices.resultBody: Move sessions out of process memory so instances can die and be replaced.

choices.label: More retries
choices.resultBody: Retries cannot recreate in-memory sessions after a crash.

choices.label: More CPU
choices.resultBody: CPU does not make in-process session state survivable.

hints: A crash must not wipe users.

incidents.title: Hot service with no redundancy
incidents.brief: One search service handles every request while other instances sit unused.
incidents.constraint: The entry path still targets a single endpoint.
incidents.question: How do you improve resilience?

choices.label: Fleet routing
choices.resultBody: Distribute requests to the fleet and drop single-host routing.

choices.label: Static DNS
choices.resultBody: Static DNS keeps every client on the same host.

choices.label: Bigger CPU
choices.resultBody: More CPU on one search node is not redundancy.

incidents.title: Social traffic burst
incidents.brief: A social mention spikes traffic. The pool is small; one instance cannot keep up.
incidents.constraint: No instance is stateful and one instance can no longer keep up.
incidents.question: What makes this resilient?

choices.label: Add instances
choices.resultBody: Add more stateless instances behind a shared entry route.

choices.label: Longer TTL
choices.resultBody: TTL on assets does not add app CPU for live requests.

choices.label: Hide with cache
choices.resultBody: Caching hides reads; this instance is CPU-bound on live work.

incidents.title: Long-running job fan-out
incidents.brief: New files are processed one at a time, so latency grows with each upload.
incidents.constraint: Work is serial and CPU-bound on a single instance.
incidents.question: What is the cleanest fix?

choices.label: Parallel workers
choices.resultBody: Parallelize work across multiple stateless workers.

choices.label: Deeper queue
choices.resultBody: A deeper queue stores delay. It does not process files faster.

choices.label: Giant machine
choices.resultBody: One giant machine is still one serial pipeline.

incidents.title: Election-day traffic surge
incidents.brief: A live event starts and one public API instance exceeds 100% CPU.
incidents.constraint: The event is short but intense; capacity must be elastic.
incidents.question: How do you prepare?

choices.label: Pre-scale fleet
choices.resultBody: Stand up multiple stateless app instances before the event and route to them.

choices.label: Keep one box
choices.resultBody: One box will not survive an election-night spike.

choices.label: Browser queue
choices.resultBody: Queueing in the browser does not add origin CPU.

incidents.title: Chat gateway saturates
incidents.brief: A realtime chat gateway holds 80,000 sockets on one process. CPU climbs past 90% every evening.
incidents.constraint: Connection state lives in that process, so extra machines cannot accept sockets yet.
incidents.question: What must change first?

choices.label: Share state
choices.resultBody: Externalize connection state so more identical gateways can share sockets.

choices.label: Raise timeouts
choices.resultBody: Longer timeouts keep more dead sockets on the same box.

choices.label: Compress chat
choices.resultBody: Compression does not move 80k sockets off one process.

hints: State is pinned to one process.
You cannot scale until state moves.

incidents.title: PDF renderer bottleneck
incidents.brief: Invoice PDFs render in the web process. p95 jumps from 200ms to 8s at month-end.
incidents.constraint: Rendering is CPU-heavy and does not need to finish inside the HTTP request.
incidents.question: How do you restore the web tier?

choices.label: PDF workers
choices.resultBody: Move rendering onto a pool of workers that scale independently of web servers.

choices.label: Bigger heap
choices.resultBody: A larger heap still burns CPU inside the request path.

choices.label: PDFs in DB
choices.resultBody: Putting PDFs in the database does not remove render CPU from the web tier.

hints: Render work is not the HTTP response.
Web and render need different scale.

incidents.title: Autoscaler never fires
incidents.brief: CPU on the only app VM sits at 85% for 20 minutes. No extra capacity appears.
incidents.constraint: The service is a single instance with no replica set defined.
incidents.question: Why does elasticity fail?

choices.label: Set replicas
choices.resultBody: Horizontal scaling needs a replica target greater than one. A single node cannot scale out.

choices.label: Bigger disk
choices.resultBody: Disk size does not create extra app processes.

choices.label: Shorter DNS
choices.resultBody: DNS TTL cannot clone a replica that does not exist.

incidents.title: Black Friday checkout
incidents.brief: Checkout is 12x normal. Two app servers both sit above 95% CPU.
incidents.constraint: The app is already stateless and sessions live in Redis.
incidents.question: What is the next capacity move?

choices.label: More instances
choices.resultBody: Add more identical checkout instances and let the entry layer spread requests.

choices.label: Logic in Redis
choices.resultBody: Checkout CPU belongs on app instances, not inside Redis.

choices.label: Pin carts
choices.resultBody: Pinning carts concentrates load again.

incidents.title: ML inference on one GPU
incidents.brief: Recommendations run on one GPU host. Queue wait time grows during a campaign.
incidents.constraint: Models are stateless at request time and can run on any replica.
incidents.question: How do you absorb inference load?

choices.label: More GPUs
choices.resultBody: Run multiple identical inference replicas and distribute requests.

choices.label: One giant batch
choices.resultBody: A bigger batch on the same GPU increases wait time.

choices.label: Infer in DB
choices.resultBody: The database cannot replace GPU inference.

incidents.title: WebSocket fan-out on one node
incidents.brief: A live sports service pushes updates from one node to every client.
incidents.constraint: A node crash drops every live connection.
incidents.question: How do you cut blast radius?

choices.label: Fan-out fleet
choices.resultBody: Run several fan-out nodes and share pub/sub so any node can serve clients.

choices.label: Fastest box
choices.resultBody: The fastest machine is still a single node for every socket.

choices.label: Memory only
choices.resultBody: Process memory makes a crash worse, not better.

hints: Every socket is on one node.

incidents.title: Cron on the app server
incidents.brief: A daily report job runs inside the only app process and saturates CPU for 40 minutes.
incidents.constraint: User traffic shares that process and p99 explodes during the job.
incidents.question: How do you protect interactive traffic?

choices.label: Job workers
choices.resultBody: Move the job to a separately scaled worker fleet so web instances stay on requests.

choices.label: Run cron more
choices.resultBody: Running the cron more often steals even more request CPU.

choices.label: 40m timeout
choices.resultBody: A 40-minute timeout is not a capacity plan.

hints: Batch work shares the web process.

incidents.title: Sticky sessions block scale-out
incidents.brief: You added four app servers, but most users still land on the original node.
incidents.constraint: Session affinity is based on in-memory session IDs.
incidents.question: What unblocks horizontal scale?

choices.label: Shared sessions
choices.resultBody: Store sessions outside the process so any instance can serve any user.

choices.label: More cookies
choices.resultBody: More sticky cookies pin even more users to one node.

choices.label: More RAM
choices.resultBody: RAM on the original node does not move sessions.

incidents.title: Search indexer cannot keep up
incidents.brief: Document ingest is 3x faster than a single indexer can write.
incidents.constraint: Indexing work is independent per document.
incidents.question: What restores ingest rate?

choices.label: More indexers
choices.resultBody: Run multiple identical indexers consuming the same ingest queue.

choices.label: Pause uploads
choices.resultBody: Pausing uploads hides the bottleneck; it does not index faster.

choices.label: Index in request
choices.resultBody: Indexing on the request path steals interactive latency.

incidents.title: Failover region too small
incidents.brief: Primary region dies. The secondary has one app instance and overloads immediately.
incidents.constraint: Failover traffic is the full production load.
incidents.question: What should have been in place?

choices.label: Warm fleet
choices.resultBody: Keep multiple scaled-out instances in the failover region, not a single warm box.

choices.label: Bigger disk
choices.resultBody: Disk size in the secondary region does not absorb request CPU.

choices.label: One XL VM
choices.resultBody: One oversized VM is still one overload domain under full failover.
